monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the air feel thick and wet inside my small map. I cannot tend my place again; the work waits until tomorrow. Here, nine things stand crowded while The Shaded Dot waits in the ruin, heavy and new. I remember the fat dot slipping before the box tilted, but now I must ask if Lype's heavy top edge feels like a lid or just empty space. If the air is empty, I will build a lid to press down on the slip. For now, I simply lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot, swapping the curve for a flat rock again, hoping the lean still holds while the house hums steady.

action.why: I need to see if the air Lype talks about is really heavy or just empty.

work.text: Bring me a photo of the sky right now, so I can see if the roof I live under is a heavy lid or just empty space.
